title: The page-writer check finds the writer by its triage tag, not by a fixed session id
why: The pick guard (#3093) keys the page writer to a fixed session id. A new triage session gets a new id, so the key goes stale and the guard refuses the real writer. hooks/feedback_guard.py is_writer ignores the key, so the two checks can disagree on who the writer is.
source: lane pick-guard-cloud-writer notes 2 and 3, via coordinator 00:13 CST Nov 13
note: One home for "who writes the page": read the session tagged cs-build:triage and cs-repo:<repo> (get_session or list_sessions), and have is_writer and the pick guard call it. Red tests first: (a) a new triage session id passes, (b) is_writer and the pick guard agree. Unmeasured: whether a container restart (same session id, new worker) also stales the key; triage restarted three times tonight with the same id. 07:24 CST Nov 13: lane session_013NEJL3DLEFY5vfbyG8CQ44 handed in PR #3124 (head 62c1d5d89). Follow-ups out of scope: step tag-writer-skips-archived; two triage sessions split across has_more pages read as one (low, note only); stale text in decision questions-go-to-owner line 22, debt layout-writer-key-stale, project-ops template operating-model lines 119-120; layout.page_writer_key has no reader; TRIAGE_TAG re-spells shared_names BUILD_TAG. Unmeasured: a container restart staling the old key.
